title: Three-Line Definition Shape Description
pattern: Writing multiple lines of text to describe the inner components of a tuple or map structure in detail.
why_bad: Inefficient layout. A single clear layout comment mapping keys to values is faster to scan, more compact, and easier to keep aligned.
detection: Comments on type definitions spanning multiple lines, detailing the sequential types in a generic structure.
counterexample: A compact single-line layout comment ('// CategoryType -> (score, weight)') or a struct with named fields.
fix: Condense the multi-line description into a single-line structural representation, or define a custom struct with named fields.
source: Dustin Boswell & Trevor Foucher, *The Art of Readable Code* (2012), Chapter 6 ("Keep Comments Compact").
